Why do we never go to a temple empty-handed? Even a banana. A flower. A spoon of sugar. As the story goes, Krishna had a best friend at school, Sudama.
Years later, Krishna was the king of Dwarka. And Sudama was so poor, his children went to bed hungry. His wife said, go and see your friend.
But Sudama had nothing to give. So she tied a handful of flattened rice in an old cloth. At the palace gates, the guards laughed at him.
But Krishna came running out, barefoot, and hugged him. Sudama was too shy to give his tiny gift. So Krishna grabbed it, and ate it like a feast.

Wait, did Sudama ask for help? Not a word. He walked home with nothing. But where his hut stood, there was now a palace. That's why we never go empty-handed. It is not the size of the gift. It is the love. Send this to your oldest friend, and comment Sudama.
